resolvedFacts.fact: Act 691 is enacted and current source review records its official status/date as Act 691 of 2025, dated 2025-04-16.
Act 691 adds §16-90-1601 and §16-90-1602; §16-90-1601(6) includes a veterans treatment specialty court program.
Act 691 repeals §16-101-106; the old text below the repeal heading is bill markup, not operative law.
The held ACIC petition and order binaries are exact, source-bound official form artifacts dated 2021-07-27: petition 5 pages and order 4 pages.
The held pair states a deferred/no-judgment-of-guilt probation or court-supervision fact pattern and includes completion/recommendation, old cross-court, service and judge-owned fields.
The current ACIC publication observation lists the old pair under its old citations; publication does not establish statutory currency or product permission.

proposedRules.topic: current route identity and stale citations
proposedRules.proposal: Treat the route as an Arkansas veterans treatment specialty-court route under A.C.A. §16-101-101 et seq., with the dismissal/sealing authority mapped to Act 691 §§16-90-1601(6) and 16-90-1602. Do not present §16-101-106 as operative law. Preserve the exact July 27, 2021 ACIC petition/order binaries as official source artifacts, but require an owner/counsel-approved form strategy before correcting, overlaying or explaining their printed citations. The petition prayer citing §16-98-303 is withheld from any product-facing legal explanation until separately resolved as a stale drug-court citation.
productTreatmentIfAdopted: route label uses §16-90-1601/§16-90-1602 mapping
source citation discrepancy is disclosed as a source-form issue
no silent mutation of either held official PDF
no packet or guide release until the citation strategy is adopted

basis.rule: Act 691 section 14 repeals §16-101-106; section 7 adds §16-90-1601 and §16-90-1602; the held forms still print §16-101-106, §16-90-1401 and the petition prints §16-98-303.
basis.observation: The statutory replacement is factually established, while the permissible participant-facing treatment of the stale official form text is a governance decision.
limits: This draft does not authorize a citation overlay, source edit, packet build or legal release.

proposedRules.topic: completion, prosecutor recommendation and judge finding
proposedRules.proposal: Require evidence of successful specialty-court completion and a prosecuting-attorney recommendation for dismissal and sealing. Keep the criminal-history consideration and appropriateness determination as judge-owned controls: the product may explain that §16-90-1602(a) requires them, but must not prefill, attest to or convert the source order’s rehabilitation checkbox into that judicial finding. A current form or separate current-law statement is needed if the official order does not supply the required finding.
productTreatmentIfAdopted: participant supplies completion evidence and date
prosecutor recommendation remains a required handoff
judge considers criminal history and appropriateness; product leaves that finding blank
no automatic approval from a rehabilitation selection

basis.rule: Act 691 §16-90-1602(a) requires successful completion, prosecuting-attorney recommendation, and the judge’s consideration of past criminal history plus determination that dismissal/sealing are appropriate.
basis.observation: Both held forms ask for completion and prosecutor recommendation; the order separately has a HAS/HAS NOT rehabilitated checkbox but no explicit current-law finding in the extracted text.
limits: Whether the official order is legally sufficient and whether a companion current-law statement is allowed remain owner/counsel questions.

proposedRules.proposal: Scope the held ACIC pair to the pre-adjudication fact pattern it actually states: deferred proceedings without a judgment of guilt followed by probation/court supervision. Do not infer post-adjudication coverage merely because the specialty-court program authority can encompass both program forms. Until an owner/counsel decision identifies a current post-adjudication instrument or approves a separate product branch, a post-adjudication participant receives a stop/handback rather than this pair.
productTreatmentIfAdopted: stage 1 describes program participation without deciding eligibility
stage 2 asks for the pre-adjudication facts printed in the pair
post-adjudication cases are withheld pending a separate current instrument and rule mapping

basis.rule: The held petition and order state deferred proceedings without a judgment of guilt and probation/court supervision. The existing source review records Act 58 §16-101-102(e) as allowing a veterans treatment specialty court program to be pre-adjudication or post-adjudication.
basis.observation: The pair’s factual scope is narrower than the program concept recorded in the source review.
limits: The Act 58 binary was not re-acquired for this draft; no post-adjudication instrument is asserted or inferred.

proposedRules.topic: separate previous offense and same-level cross-court relief
proposedRules.proposal: Withhold the separate-previous-offense branch until mapped to Act 691 §16-90-1602(d). If adopted, require the specialty-court judge’s court level, the other conviction court’s same-level status, successful specialty-court completion, completion of the other sentence, the other court’s agreement that sealing is appropriate, and that court’s signature on the ACIC uniform sealing order. Do not treat the old target-group checkbox, four old exclusions or generic concurrence language as the current contract without an owner/counsel mapping. Keep all other-court and judge fields blank unless supplied by those actors.
productTreatmentIfAdopted: separate offense is a conditional branch with explicit stop conditions
same-level court and completed-other-sentence facts are required
uniform-order signature is a court-owned prerequisite
old target-group/exclusion text is retained as historical source content until mapped

basis.rule: Act 691 §16-90-1602(d) requires completion of the specialty program, completion of the other court sentence, and the other court’s agreement plus signature on the ACIC uniform sealing order, with circuit/district same-level jurisdiction.
basis.observation: The held forms’ optional branch asks about another circuit court, target-group status, four exclusions and concurrence, but does not establish the newer same-level/completed-sentence/uniform-order contract.
limits: No automated cross-court approval, old-exclusion waiver or judge concurrence may be invented.

proposedRules.topic: immediate order, prior felony count and DWI/BWI guard
proposedRules.proposal: If adopted into participant guidance, state only the enacted Act 691 treatment: sealing follows the Comprehensive Criminal Record Sealing Act procedures, a specialty-court judge may enter the order immediately upon completion, and the route has no limit on previous felony convictions under §16-90-1406(c)(1). Preserve a separate stop for DWI/BWI offenses until the applicable §5-65-111 lookback periods have elapsed; do not read the removal of the prior-felony-count limit as eliminating other statutory conditions.
productTreatmentIfAdopted: immediate-order permission is described as a court authority, not a participant guarantee
prior-felony count is not used as an automatic disqualifier for this route
DWI/BWI remains withheld until the statutory lookback condition is met

basis.rule: Act 691 §16-90-1602(b) provides immediate sealing upon completion and removes the §16-90-1406(c)(1) previous-felony limit; §16-90-1602(c) retains a DWI/BWI lookback restriction.
basis.observation: These rules are absent from the held pair’s printed text and therefore require a governed guidance treatment.
limits: No eligibility result is made for a person with prior felonies or a DWI/BWI record.

proposedRules.proposal: Keep program admission and completion as a separate stage-1 evidence gate. Before stage-2 generation, require the owner-approved source of adult status, veteran/service-member status, qualifying disorder and policy-compliance facts recorded in the existing source review’s Act 58 citation, together with completion evidence. The two held forms’ completion date, case details and status questions are insufficient by themselves to establish all program eligibility elements.
productTreatmentIfAdopted: stage 1 collects or verifies only owner-approved program records
stage 2 refuses when eligibility evidence is absent or conflicts
the petition/order is never treated as proof of program eligibility merely because it contains a completion statement

basis.rule: The source review records Act 58 §16-101-103 eligibility elements; the held pair asks for completion, case facts and status facts but not all listed admission/eligibility elements.
basis.observation: The current product boundary between program participation and post-completion filing is explicit in the existing source review.
limits: The Act 58 source was not independently re-sourced in this bounded draft; this is a proposed input contract, not a legal determination.

proposedRules.proposal: Do not publish the historical three-day service or thirty-day objection timing as current product guidance until a current procedural record confirms it. Preserve the held petition’s certificate-of-service recipients (prosecuting or city attorney and arresting agency) and the order’s transmission list (ACIC, Administrative Office of the Courts, prosecuting/city attorney, district clerk if applicable and arresting agency) as source observations only. A current adopted rule must reconcile those lists with §16-90-1602(b)’s incorporation of Comprehensive Criminal Record Sealing Act procedures and identify which actors/timings are mandatory.
productTreatmentIfAdopted: service recipients remain a participant/court handoff
historical timing appears only with an approved current authority
no notice deadline or service completion is prefilled
the order’s agency transmission language is not treated as proof that the participant completed service

basis.rule: The held petition contains the certificate-of-service language; the held order contains the certified-copy transmission list and cites §16-90-1413. Act 691 §16-90-1602(b) incorporates the Comprehensive Criminal Record Sealing Act procedures.
basis.observation: The reviewed authorities do not establish that the memo’s three-day/30-day language remains the current procedural contract.
limits: No current fee/service procedural source was acquired for this draft.

proposedRules.proposal: Leave the petition filing fee and any petition fee-waiver route unresolved and unquoted until a current clerk/ACIC or owner-approved procedural authority is bound. Keep veterans-treatment program costs or indigency waivers separate from a post-completion sealing-petition filing fee. Do not infer a fee or waiver from the held forms’ absence of a fee field.
productTreatmentIfAdopted: fee is a required factual input only after current authority is bound
waiver is a conditional handoff with its own authority and recipient
program-cost waiver and petition filing-fee waiver are separate concepts
no fee amount, waiver eligibility or waiver outcome is generated here

basis.rule: The source review states that the pair does not state a filing fee or fee waiver and that Act 58 §16-101-104 addresses program costs/fees rather than a definitive petition fee.
basis.observation: The forms do not supply a current fee schedule or waiver mechanism.
limits: No fee assumption or waiver clearance is authorized by this draft.

explicitScopeLimits: Only ar-veterans-court-set and its two-stage process are covered; no Act 346 work, other Arkansas routes or generic sealing route is changed.
This draft proposes product treatment from existing evidence. It is not an owner adoption, counsel opinion, court approval, packet verdict, source-freshness certification or production grant.
The two held PDFs remain immutable source artifacts. No PDF, source receipt, builder, field map, guidance, shared registry, queue, claim ledger or manifest was edited.
The public ACIC page observation proves that the old pair was published when observed; it does not cure stale citations or authorize a corrected participant surface.
No post-adjudication branch, separate-offense approval, service deadline, fee amount, waiver outcome, program eligibility result or judicial finding is inferred.
No current owner/counsel adoption can be inferred from Act 691, the source review or source custody.
